artists.biography:
Steven Wilson (born 1967 in Kingston upon Thames, England) is a singer, songwriter, guitarist, multi-instrumentalist, and producer best known as the founder and creative force behind Porcupine Tree. Formed in 1987, the project evolved from Wilson’s home-studio experiments into a major progressive rock band, blending psychedelia, ambient music, electronics, art rock, and progressive metal. Albums such as In Absentia, Deadwing, and Fear of a Blank Planet established Porcupine Tree for their intricate arrangements, dark psychological themes, and meticulously produced sound. Wilson has also worked with No-Man, Blackfield, and Storm Corrosion.

Wilson began his solo career with Insurgentes in 2008, expanding his musical language through atmospheric rock, experimental textures, and sophisticated songwriting. His notable releases include the double album Grace for Drowning, The Raven That Refused to Sing (And Other Stories), Hand. Cannot. Erase., To the Bone, The Future Bites, and The Harmony Codex. Beyond performing, he is respected for remastering and remixing classic albums by artists including King Crimson, Jethro Tull, Yes, and Tears for Fears, helping introduce progressive and art-rock recordings to new generations. His career has made him one of the leading modern figures in progressive music.

perplexity.description:
Requiem For A Village is Steven Wilson’s ninth studio album, released through Fiction Records as a richly atmospheric entry in his progressive-rock catalogue. The record balances expansive, carefully layered arrangements with concise melodic writing, drawing on Wilson’s characteristic blend of art rock, psychedelia, electronics, and cinematic instrumental texture. Its title track and “On Chapel Slope” suggest a reflective, pastoral mood, with the album’s themes and sound world evoking memory, place, and the gradual erosion of familiar landscapes.

The oxblood edition is a limited two-record vinyl pressing of the 2026 album, offering a collectible presentation of Wilson’s latest studio work. Alongside the standard black-vinyl version, it reflects the strong physical-product focus surrounding the release, while preserving the detailed dynamics and immersive sequencing that make Wilson’s albums particularly rewarding on vinyl.
